title: Kniffel – rules
h1sub: Dice game rules & how to play
sub: Five dice, three rolls per turn, thirteen boxes on the score sheet: the dice classic for 1 to 6 players. Read it once, roll, done.

seo.rulesT: Kniffel Rules – How to Play the Dice Game
seo.rulesD: Kniffel explained: rolling and keeping dice, all 13 boxes of the score sheet, the 35-point bonus, striking a box, scoring and variants.

goal: The goal: Fill all 13 boxes of your score sheet with the best possible rolls and end the game with the most points.

info.label: Fact sheet
info.gearAlt: Five dice, a score sheet and a pen
info.intro: Kniffel takes five minutes to explain and is fun for everyone from kids to grandparents. Luck decides every roll, but if you keep the right dice and choose your boxes wisely, you’ll win more often. All you need is five dice and a piece of paper.

setupLead: You don’t need much, and a round with friends takes about half an hour.
setup1: 5 dice – ideally with a dice cup.
setup2: One score sheet per player with the 13 boxes from this page (any piece of paper will do) and a pen.
setup3: 1 to 6 players. Alone, you play for your high score.
setupP: Everyone rolls once with all five dice: the highest total starts. Play goes clockwise, and the game lasts exactly 13 rounds – one for every box.
turnLead: On your turn you roll up to three times. After that you must write a score in one box.
s1p: Your first roll always uses all five dice.
s2p: Put aside the dice you want to keep and roll the rest again. You may do this twice. Dice you kept may go back into the cup on the next roll.
s3p: After the third roll at the latest, choose one free box and enter the points. You may also stop earlier.
exAlt: Three rolls: first three fives are kept, then the 3 and 6 are rolled again, in the end there are four fives and a 2.
exP: Mia keeps her three 5s and rolls the other two dice twice. In the end she has four 5s and a 2. Now she can choose: Fives for 20 points, or Four of a kind for 22. A box once filled can’t be used again.
strikeP: You must write something down every turn. If no box fits your roll, enter 0 in a box of your choice – that box is “struck” for the rest of the game. Good boxes to sacrifice are Ones or Kniffel when time is running out.
upLead: In the upper section you only count the dice with that number.
upP: Example: you roll 4 4 4 2 6 and write it under Fours – that’s 12 points. The figure on the right shows the target: three of each number.
bonusP: Bonus: If the upper section adds up to 63 or more, you get 35 extra points. That’s exactly three of every number – one more six can make up for a missing one.
lowLead: In the lower section, the pattern of the dice counts. Gold dice are the ones that matter.
lb_threeP: At least three dice show the same number. Score the total of all five dice.
lb_fourP: At least four dice show the same number. Score the total of all five dice.
lb_fullP: Three of one number and two of another. Always 25 points.
lb_smallP: Four numbers in a row: 1‑2‑3‑4, 2‑3‑4‑5 or 3‑4‑5‑6. The fifth die doesn’t matter. 30 points.
lb_largeP: Five numbers in a row: 1‑2‑3‑4‑5 or 2‑3‑4‑5‑6. 40 points.
lb_kniffelP: All five dice show the same number. The best box: 50 points.
lb_chanceP: Anything goes. Score the total of all five dice – your safety net for a bad roll.
scoreLead: When all 13 boxes are filled, add up your score sheet:
endP: After 13 rounds everyone has filled every box. The player with the highest grand total wins. A tie? Then share the win – or play a quick decider: one roll each, highest total wins.
varLead: Kniffel is played slightly differently at every table. Agree before the first roll which of these rules you use:
var1: Extra Kniffels: If you roll another Kniffel after the Kniffel box is already filled with 50, you get 50 bonus points each time.
var2: Joker rule: An extra Kniffel can be used as a joker for Full house, Small or Large straight and scores the full points there – but only if the matching box of the upper section is already filled.
var3: Top to bottom: Fill the boxes strictly in order from Ones to Chance. A lot more luck, a lot less planning.
var4: Blind: Before your first roll, announce the box you’re playing for. Wrong? Then you score 0 there.
var5: Triple Kniffel: Each player has three columns; the second counts double, the third triple. 39 rounds – for long evenings.
var6: Saved rolls: Rolls you don’t use can be saved for a later turn (at most 3 in total).
var7: Yatzy rules: The Scandinavian version also has One pair and Two pairs, a Small straight is only 1‑2‑3‑4‑5 (15 points), a Large one only 2‑3‑4‑5‑6 (20), and the upper bonus is 50.
faq1q: Do I have to roll three times?
faq1a: No. You may stop after the first or second roll and write down your score straight away.
faq2q: Can I pick up dice I already put aside?
faq2a: Yes. Before each roll you decide again which dice you keep and which go back into the cup.
faq3q: Does a large straight also count as a small straight?
faq3a: Yes. 1‑2‑3‑4‑5 contains four numbers in a row, so you may enter it as a Small straight for 30 – useful if the Large straight is already filled.
faq4q: Is a Kniffel also a Full house?
faq4a: By the basic rules, no: a Full house needs two different numbers. With the joker rule (see Variants) an extra Kniffel can count as a Full house.
faq5q: Can I write a score in a box that doesn’t fit?
faq5a: Only as a 0. That’s called striking the box, and you can’t use it again in this game.
faq6q: What is the highest possible score?
faq6a: Without extra Kniffels it’s 375 points: 105 in the upper section (five of each number), 35 bonus and 235 in the lower section.
faq7q: Is Kniffel the same as Yahtzee?
faq7a: Almost. Yahtzee is the American name, Yatzy the Scandinavian one; the boxes are basically the same, but bonuses and straights differ a little (see Variants). Kniffel and Yahtzee are also trademarks of commercial dice games; this page explains how to play with five ordinary dice.
faq8q: How do I get better at Kniffel?
faq8a: Aim for the 63 bonus early: three 5s or 6s in the upper section are worth a lot. Keep Chance as long as possible for an emergency, and strike Ones rather than an expensive box.
